subject: MedStream hosting path & audit evidence follow-up
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Aditi Shah <aditi.shah@medstreamhealth.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@medstreamhealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + hosting options & initial evidence asks

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today — great conversation. Per our call, I wanted to recap where we landed and outline concrete next steps so your security and procurement teams have an actionable list. TL;DR: we can support all three hosting modes, but the right path depends on PHI scope, audit timelines, and your encryption/KMS requirements.

Quick summary of hosting options (tradeoffs we discussed):
- Hosted API (fastest): Redwood-managed; best time-to-value. Requires a signed BAA and SOC2 evidence. Good when PHI processing is limited to predictable request types and you can accept standard network egress controls.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool): Customer-dedicated tenancy within our infra; provides stronger isolation and predictable throughput. Often chosen when customers need stricter data separation but still want a managed control plane.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Full customer VPC or on-prem package; recommended when you must control keys (HSM/KMS) or when your auditors require explicit network isolation / no egress to shared control plane.

From a compliance perspective, your asks today were: BAA, SOC2 Type II evidence, audit log retention windows, and a network diagram showing egress/ingress. Please confirm the items below so we can propose a recommended path and timeline:
1) Will MedStream be processing PHI? (Yes/No) — I know you said likely yes for the pilot, please confirm scope (fields/types).
2) SOC2 requirement: do you need the full Type II report (redacted) or is our SOC2 summary plus control mapping adequate for initial procurement?
3) Key management: do you require customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) or is Redwood-managed KMS acceptable?
4) Expected traffic: monthly API calls and average request size (tokens) — helps sizing for Dedicated.
5) Target audit window / procurement deadline (approx date) so we can prioritize artifacts and DSAT.

Next steps from Redwood: I’m attaching a BAA draft and a short SOC2 evidence checklist we typically hand to procurement. I’ll loop Sean and Marissa (security/solutions) for technical clarifications. Proposed follow-up: 30-min audit-evidence call Friday 9/4 at 11:00 PT — does that work for your team?

Attachments (stubs): BAA_draft.docx (initial draft) ; SOC2_2025_TypeII_summary.pdf (control mapping) ; network_diagram_request.png (template we request)

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Aditi Shah <aditi.shah@medstreamhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@medstreamhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + hosting options & initial evidence asks

Thanks Neha — that recap is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:
- Confirmed: MedStream will process PHI for the pilot (patient identifiers + clinical notes). We need a BAA in place before any PHI flows.
- SOC2: our security team typically requests the full SOC2 Type II report (redacted is acceptable) for the last audit period. If you can provide the 2025 Type II report, that would be ideal.
- Keys: we prefer customer-controlled KMS for encryption-at-rest (bring-your-own-key) for the production environment. For a short pilot we could evaluate Redwood-managed KMS if it reduces time-to-value, but production will require customer keys.
- Traffic estimate (pilot): ~150k inference calls/month, avg payload ~600 tokens; potential scale to 1M+/mo in 6–9 months.
- Procurement timeline: we are aiming to complete security review by 2026-09-30 and sign procurement by mid-October.

Two asks: can you share a sample network diagram (egress/ingress, control plane endpoints) and your pen-test/third-party attestation summary? Also, do you support isolating dedicated capacity into our AWS account (VPC peering or similar) or only into a Redwood-managed VPC?

If you can get the SOC2 report and pen test summary to us by EOD 9/3, that will help our security lead begin mapping controls. We can push the 9/4 call to next week if needed — but earlier is better.

Thanks,
Aditi Shah
Director, Security & Compliance
MedStream Health
aditi.shah@medstreamhealth.com | (202) 555-0144

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: MedStream security asks — technical recommendation

Looping in a quick technical assessment based on Aditi’s reply:
- Given PHI and the procurement timeline, Private VPC (customer VPC or on-prem) is the conservative recommendation for production because you requested BYOK/KMS and stronger network isolation.
- Recommended interim path: start pilot on Dedicated capacity with a scoped BAA and strict egress rules while MedStream completes SOC2 review. This lets them validate models and traffic patterns without the full on-prem lift. If they decide production needs BYOK, we migrate to Private VPC — migration path is supported but requires ~3–6 weeks for network and key integrations.

Required artifacts and notes for procurement (we should send these to Aditi):
1) Redacted SOC2 Type II report (2025) — full report preferred, otherwise our SOC2 summary + control mapping.
2) Penetration test / third-party attestation summary (most recent within 18 months).
3) BAA — editable Word doc (we have a template; Neha sent draft).
4) Network diagram template + sample showing control plane endpoints, port/IP ranges, and egress flows.
5) KMS integration docs and HSM options (we support both customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS and on-prem HSM with private deployments).
6) Audit log retention: confirm default 90 days, configurable up to customer-specified retention with export.

Notes for the proposal: if they need BYOK in production, call out the extra procurement milestone (KMS proof-of-concept) and the timeline delta. For Dedicated -> Private migration we should price the migration and flag a one-time setup fee.

I’ll attach our SOC2 summary and a short network guidance doc for Neha to send.

—Sean
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Aditi Shah <aditi.shah@medstreamhealth.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@medstreamhealth.com>

Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 11:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + hosting options & initial evidence asks

Aditi / Raj — thanks for the quick reply and timeline. Per Sean’s note, attaching the items that should get you through the procurement intake:
- BAA_draft.docx (editable) — please flag any redlines; we can get legal involved quickly.
- SOC2_2025_TypeII_summary.pdf (redaction-friendly summary + control mapping) — full redacted report available on request (we’ll prepare a secure share).
- network_diagram_request.png (template) — fill this out with your network team; we’ll review in the call.

To your question about Dedicated isolation: we can allocate Dedicated capacity within a Redwood-managed VPC with strict tenant isolation. For tighter isolation, we offer a Private VPC deployment where we either deploy into a customer VPC (VPC peering / PrivateLink pattern) or provide an on-prem package. I’ve noted your BYOK requirement — for production we’ll plan for customer-managed KMS. For the pilot we can offer a temporary Redwood-managed KMS if that speeds the POC, but keys would need to be rotated/migrated before production.

Proposed immediate actions:
- Aditi: confirm PHI fields (short list) and whether the pilot can run with Redwood-managed KMS for initial testing.
- Raj: coordinate with your network team to complete the network diagram template and share by 9/3 EOD.
- Neha/Redwood: we’ll prepare a secure share for the redacted SOC2 report and produce the pen-test summary (expected by EOD 9/3).

I’ll hold 11:00 PT on 9/4 as a tentative follow-up; please let me know if you prefer a different slot.

Attachments (stubs): BAA_draft.docx ; SOC2_2025_TypeII_summary.pdf ; network_diagram_request.png

Thanks — Neha
